source.title: Similarity: generalizations, applications and open problems

accepted.question_text: For nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation models and their higher-order generalizations in which a finite-time singularity occurs, so that the solution or some of its partial derivatives diverge, can one develop general rigorous methods to determine the stability of local self-similar solutions describing behavior near the singularity, especially in high-order models where the possible local self-similar solutions may form a countably infinite set?
accepted.context_brief: stability of local self-similar singularity profiles

evidence.quote: stability properties must be studied on a case-by-case basis

accepted.question_text: For partial differential equation models whose ultimate evolution is long-time behavior or behavior close to a finite-time singularity, what role do quasi-self-similar solutions, meaning solutions that satisfy the governing equations asymptotically rather than exactly, play in describing that evolution, and how should their analysis combine similarity methods, dynamical-systems methods, perturbation methods, and numerical methods?

Can modern symmetry approaches be developed into systematic symmetry-based techniques for identifying candidate intermediate-asymptotic solutions of partial differential equations, in the setting where similarity solutions are used to describe intermediate-asymptotic behavior for wide classes of PDEs?

needs_review.question_text_raw: open problems relating to the Similarity areas 2.1-2.6
